A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PanoGrounder. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding experiments, cross-dataset and text generalization results, ablations, qualitative analyses and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds zero-shot comparisons, reconstruction and deployment experiments, backbone evaluations and diagnostic analyses.

M1.justification: The stated geometric adapter band changes from [L/3,2L/3] to [L/3,2L/3), removing the shared endpoint with the semantic band (v1 Section 3.3; v2 Section 3.2). The core pipeline and objectives remain intact. Axis-based geometric QA was already documented in v1 Appendix A.4.

E1.justification: v2 adds grounding under fully automated RGB-only reconstruction without ground-truth meshes or camera trajectories, plus a new self-captured living-room demonstration (Appendices C.1 and D.2). These substantially extend tested input conditions beyond the benchmark reconstructions in v1; the principal named benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: New Table 2 compares against ZSVG3D, SeeGround and VLM-Grounder in zero-shot Nr3D evaluation. Appendix D.1 adds LLaVA-3D to the resource comparison. Conversely, TSP3D is removed from Table 1. These change actual comparator participation, beyond citation or naming edits.

E3.justification: v2 restricts the representation comparison to 92 of 141 validation scenes, requiring at least 300 COLMAP-registered images, and evaluates automatic reconstructions with the existing 3DGS checkpoint. It also introduces zero-shot, smaller-backbone and linear-probe protocols. The text-variant table's metric changes from Acc@0.25 to Top-1, with unchanged values; this does not establish a rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an all-feature control without EMD, inference-time geometry masking, adapter-layer ablations and linear probes, scene-size/category/elevation analyses, backbone scalability tests and explicit failure cases. Existing camera-placement, initialization, convergence and rotation analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Appendix C.2 introduces a linear fit and correlation reporting for floor area versus camera count (r=0.80), adding a statistical estimation procedure absent from v1. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Retained headline scores are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results, including 53.2 zero-shot Nr3D accuracy and 52.1 ScanRefer accuracy with Qwen2.5-VL-7B. The representation comparison replaces v1's ScanRefer 3DGS/mesh scores of 59.3/61.0 with 60.8/61.6 on the restricted subset and adds automatic 3DGS at 55.1; these are not same-setting gains. Nr3D/Sr3D representation results are removed, while new diagnostic, resource and qualitative outcomes are added.

T1.justification: The camera-scoring, cross-view consistency, aggregation and weighted digit-EMD mathematics are retained. v2 explicitly writes the standard cross-entropy formula and clarifies notation, without adding a substantive derivation, theoretical assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The panoramic-interface, ScanRefer/Nr3D performance and generalization claims remain. v2's introduction explicitly extends the applicability claim to casually captured RGB frames with off-the-shelf reconstruction. Its conclusion also omits v1's explicit open-vocabulary characterization.

C2.justification: v1's limitations paragraph mainly lists future tasks; v2 explicitly discusses reconstruction dependence, noise sensitivity and slower VLM inference. Added analyses explain ambiguous-reference, occlusion and partial-object failures, interpret backbone tradeoffs, and qualify the adapter design by finding exact mid/late placement noncritical (Appendices C–E).

D1.justification: v2 newly documents ground-truth initialization of the existing 3DGS variant, automatic reconstruction and checkpoint reuse, detailed QA supervision, smartphone capture specifications, 30K reconstruction steps, and stage-level CPU/GPU memory and timing. These substantially expand deployment and reproducibility information. The five-epoch training budget was already disclosed in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds SpatialRGPT, COLMAP and visual-representation analysis citations while pruning works including SAT, LAR, ScanReason and TSP3D. Related work more explicitly contrasts curated 3D inputs, limited viewing coverage and specialized 3D tokens with PanoGrounder, while retaining the original central research positioning.

P1.justification: Substantial passages in the introduction, related work and method are rewritten. Panorama construction and adapters are merged into one subsection, benchmark discussion is consolidated, pinhole comparisons move under ablations, and the appendix is reorganized around analyses and deployment. Terminology and affiliations also change.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, replaces the introductory overview, redraws pipeline and adapter diagrams, and adds numerous diagnostic and deployment displays. Two earlier appendix examples reappear in the introductory figure. The representation table is restructured, and existing mesh/3DGS images gain explanatory annotations.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for practical applicability and the contribution beyond a large backbone: it adds automatic reconstruction tests, a real capture demonstration, resource accounting, smaller-backbone comparisons and diagnostic controls. Concrete limitations and failure cases also improve transparency. The reconstruction comparison becomes narrower, excluding 49 validation scenes and dropping Nr3D/Sr3D representation results, while LIFT-GS retains its original evaluation setting. These limits constrain that comparison, but the added validation addresses important gaps in v1 and yields a substantial net improvement.
